name: RW Aurigae
description: Official test target. Young T Tauri star (A+B, 1.5" apart, unresolved): it does not move, it changes brightness. Saturated in D2–D6; measured offline on unsaturated D1 exposures at matched wavelength, it brightened by about 1 mag (0.75–0.77 µm) from Sep 2025 to Sep 2026. In the B/W blink only the D1 frames can show it (a 2.6x display-level brightness ratio between 2025W36_1A_0233_3D1 and 2026W37_1A_0234_3D1, measured on the published images); the D2–D6 cores are saturated. Brightness for science comes from the FITS light curve below, which plots those D1 measurements of the blended pair; saturation removes most exposures of the bright state.

notes: Automatic detection and catalog matching were not run.

Pixel values and stretch limits are IMAGE - ZODI (SPHEREx zodiacal model subtracted) in MJy/sr; PNGs use an asinh mapping with the same contrast for every frame of a detector, and transparent pixels mean no data. Saturated star cores that SPHEREx left empty (NaN) and detector-defect pixels (NONFUNC, HOT, COLD, PERSIST, SNOWBALL, and SUR_ERROR that is not part of a star's profile, e.g. cosmic-ray hits) are filled from their neighbours for display only; SUR_ERROR pixels on a star and finite OVERFLOW pixels are shown as recorded. All of them count as invalid in valid_fraction. Highlight roll-off where the target at the centre outshines the field's bright end (Stretch.vmax) and its core is unflagged (not saturated) in most frames: instead of clipping to white, values above vmax are compressed logarithmically into the top 15% of the grey range, so the target's brightness changes stay visible in the blink; vmax maps to 85% grey, so these detectors look 15% dimmer than the others (D1: white = vmax + 53.4 MJy/sr). thumb.png is a D5 frame.

Frame selection: downloaded 81 candidate frame(s) (up to 2 x max_frames=40) and kept 40, spread round-robin over seasons x detectors; inside each (season, detector) the frames whose wavelength at the field centre is closest to a per-detector reference (D1 0.771 um, D2 1.214 um, D3 1.681 um, D4 2.465 um, D5 3.982 um, D6 4.441 um) come first, then those nearest the season middle; frames without a known wavelength rank last. Rejected 0 bad frame(s) whose IMAGE - ZODI robust scatter exceeds 15x the noise of their VARIANCE plane (background steps) and 3x the median of the same detector's candidates (on bright nebulae every frame scatters more, so only outliers are rejected). Downloaded 52 more D2/D3 frame(s) only to find J/H/Ks wavelengths for the false-color composites; they are not blink frames.

Registration check: every frame's field stars were compared with their median position over the field's candidate frames (all detectors: a correct WCS puts a star at the same grid position at every wavelength); 81 of 81 blink candidate frame(s) and 52 of 52 J/H/Ks top-up frame(s) checked (kept: median 0.04 px, max 0.12 px). Rejected 1 misregistered frame(s) whose stars are off by more than 0.5 px (archive WCS error; they would fake a jump of the whole field), also from the false-color composites: 2026W38_1A_0162_3D6 (1.34 px).

False-color composites: 3 'detectors' and 3 'jhk' season composite(s) (infrared, not true color). detectors = full range: blue = D1 (fallback D2), green = D3 (D4), red = D6 (D5), coadds of the season's published frames. jhk = 2MASS-like: blue / green / red = coadd of the season's downloaded exposures (including unpublished candidates) within 0.06 µm of J 1.25 / H 1.65 / Ks 2.17 µm at the field centre, else the nearest one within 0.12 µm. Each channel: one weight per frame, sky removed, bad pixels left out; a pixel bad in every frame of a channel (saturated core, detector defect, ramp-fit error) is drawn neutral at the brightest channel's level, so saturated cores look white (display only). Green spans 2 sigma below the sky to the bright end of its usable pixels; red and blue are scaled to green by the median field-star flux ratio (target halo excluded), so typical bright field stars look white; limits shared by every season with the same detectors, except that a noisy channel (pixel noise above 3% of its range) has its black point set per season at its own sky + 2 sigma, so its speckle goes black (fainter field stars then look the complementary colour); colour-preserving asinh (Lupton et al. 2004).
Skipped 1 frame(s): 2026W38_1A_0162_3D6: misregistered frame: field stars 1.34 px off their consensus position
